root_cause.text: The function `mt76_connac2_mac_write_txwi_80211()` was accessing nested management frame fields (`mgmt->u.action.u.addba_req.capab`) without first validating that the skb contained sufficient data to hold those fields, allowing out-of-bounds memory access on malformed or truncated frames.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a length check `skb->len >= IEEE80211_MIN_ACTION_SIZE + 1 + 1 + 2` before accessing `mgmt->u.action.u.addba_req.capab`. This check ensures the frame is large enough to contain the action category byte, action code byte, and the 2-byte capability field. Without this check, a frame shorter than the required size would allow the code to read beyond the allocated skb buffer when dereferencing the nested structure members.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add buffer length validation to prevent out-of-bounds access when processing ADDBA_REQ action frames.
intent_record.what: Added a bounds check condition `skb->len >= IEEE80211_MIN_ACTION_SIZE + 1 + 1 + 2` to the existing multi-condition if statement that validates action frame type and category before accessing nested struct members in mgmt->u.action.u.addba_req.
intent_record.how: This change prevents out-of-bounds memory access by ensuring the skb buffer contains sufficient data before dereferencing the addba_req structure members. Without this check, the code could read past the allocated buffer if a malformed or truncated action frame is processed, potentially causing information disclosure or kernel crash.

grouping_result.intent: Add buffer length validation to prevent out-of-bounds access when processing ADDBA_REQ action frames.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly addresses the root cause by adding buffer length validation before accessing nested management frame fields in ADDBA_REQ action frames, preventing the out-of-bounds memory access vulnerability described in the root cause.

This line accesses mgmt->u.action.u.addba_req.action_code without prior buffer length validation, allowing out-of-bounds access on truncated frames that may not contain the action_code field.
This line accesses mgmt->u.action.category without validating the skb length, which could be out-of-bounds on malformed frames, though the subsequent capab access is the primary vulnerability.

On a malformed or truncated frame, this causes out-of-bounds memory access, which is the primary vulnerability.

This conditional statement accesses mgmt->u.action.u.addba_req.action_code without prior buffer length validation. On truncated frames that lack the action_code field, this access can read out-of-bounds memory.

This statement accesses mgmt->u.action.category without validating the skb length first. While less deeply nested than the capab access, it still represents an unvalidated field access that could be out-of-bounds on malformed frames.

diff --git a/drivers/net/wireless/mediatek/mt76/mt76_connac_mac.c b/driver
bic_trace_step.reason:
The function `mt76_connac2_mac_write_txwi_80211()` at lines 104-180 contains the vulnerable construct. Specifically, at lines 113-117, the code accesses nested management frame fields without validating skb length:

c
if (ieee80211_is_action(fc) &&
    mgmt->u.action.category == WLAN_CATEGORY_BACK &&
    mgmt->u.action.u.addba_req.action_code == WLAN_ACTION_ADDBA_REQ) {
    u16 capab = le16_to_cpu(mgmt->u.action.u.addba_req.capab);


The code casts `skb->data` to `struct ieee80211_mgmt *mgmt` at line 105 and then immediately accesses deeply nested fields (`mgmt->u.action.u.addba_req.capab`) without first checking that the skb contains sufficient data to hold these fields. A malformed or truncated frame could have skb->len smaller than the offset of these nested fields, causing out-of-bounds memory access. There is no `skb_len()` validation or bounds checking before accessing these nested structure members.
